---
title: "FRAP Data Analysis - Individual Curve Modeling with Bootstrap (violin y axes from 0)"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)

# minpack.lm provides nlsLM(), a Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least-squares
# fitter that's more robust to imperfect starting values than base nls() -
# used below for the exponential recovery fits.
if (!requireNamespace("minpack.lm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("minpack.lm")
}
library(minpack.lm)
```

This script works from the **individual-curve** csv files exported by the
main analysis script (`*_individual_curves.csv`, one per cell line per
replicate - one row per region, per frame), rather than the already-averaged
`*_mean_curve.csv` files. It:

1. Reads all individual-curve files across every replicate and counts how
   many individual curves (regions) are available per cell line/channel.
2. Pools every individual curve into one average recovery curve per cell
   line/channel.
3. Fits mono-, bi-, and tri-exponential recovery models to those average
   curves (for the channel(s) chosen below) and picks the best-fitting
   model (lowest AIC) for each cell line/channel.
4. For **every cell line**, runs a 1,000-iteration bootstrap: each
   iteration randomly draws (with replacement, so the same curve can be
   picked more than once) as many individual curves as are actually
   available for that cell line/channel, averages them into a resampled
   curve, and re-fits it with the model chosen in step 3. The resulting
   1,000 sets of fit parameters are then summarized as a mean ± SD per
   parameter.

Point `curve_folder` at a folder that contains the exported
`*_individual_curves.csv` files from all the replicates you want to
combine (they can come from different `export_folder`s - just copy/collect
them into one place first, or point this at a parent folder and set
`recursive <- TRUE` if they're in per-replicate subfolders).

## Parameters

```{r params}
curve_folder <- "/Volumes/lionnt01lab/lionnt01labspace/Henry/FRAP/2026_08_analyze_all_3_quick_recovery_replicates/bootstrap_analysis"   # <-- EDIT THIS
recursive    <- TRUE   # set TRUE if curve csvs are in subfolders per replicate

# --- which channel(s) to model ---
# Everything before the "Model the average recovery curves" section
# (reading files, counting curves, building average curves) is done for
# every channel present in the data. Modeling, best-fit selection, and the
# bootstrap below are restricted to the channel(s) listed here.
channels_to_model <- c("Halo-JFx650")   # <-- EDIT: e.g. c("GFP", "Halo-JFx650")

# Optional: restrict the *plots* below to specific cell lines, e.g.
# c("H2B", "CTCF"). Does not affect any computation (fitting, bootstrap,
# per-replicate fits, or the csv exports still cover every cell line) -
# only which cell lines actually get plotted. Set to NULL to plot every
# cell line present in the data.
cell_lines_to_plot <- c("HOXC10","HOXC13","SOX2","HOXC10-13-10","HOXC13-10-13")

# Restricts a vector/column of cell lines to `cell_lines_to_plot` above, if
# set; returns everything unchanged when cell_lines_to_plot is NULL. Used
# only in the plotting chunks below. Defined here (rather than alongside
# the other helpers further down) so it's available to the very first
# plotting chunk, plot-average-curves, which runs before that point.
select_cell_lines <- function(all_cell_lines) {
  if (is.null(cell_lines_to_plot)) return(all_cell_lines)
  intersect(cell_lines_to_plot, all_cell_lines)
}

# Bleach time (s): used to mark the bleach event on plots and, if this is
# left NA, to auto-detect the bleach frame for fitting (time of the
# minimum ratio). The individual-curve csv files exported by the main
# analysis script already have their time axis zeroed to the bleach event,
# so 0 is the right default if you used that script's export. Set to NA to
# auto-detect per curve instead, or to a fixed value if your files use a
# different time convention.
bleach_time <- 0

# --- bootstrap settings ---
# The bootstrap below now runs automatically for every cell line found in
# the data (no need to name one here).

# Which model to use for every bootstrap iteration - chosen manually
# rather than automatically from `best_fits`, so it stays fixed even if
# the AIC-best model changes as you tweak things upstream. Must be one of
# "mono-exponential", "bi-exponential", "tri-exponential", and must be a
# model that actually converged (in `fit_results`) for the cell
# line/channel being bootstrapped.
bootstrap_model <- "bi-exponential"   # <-- EDIT THIS if you want a different model

n_bootstrap_iterations <- 1000

# A fitted iteration is discarded if its recovery plateau (C + sum of all
# A_i) exceeds this value. Data is normalized so the pre-bleach baseline
# is ~1, so a plateau well above that usually signals a degenerate/
# non-identifiable fit (e.g. a huge amplitude paired with a near-zero rate
# constant for a poorly-resolved component) rather than a real recovery
# curve - see the A vs 1/k diagnostic plots below for how to spot these.
max_plateau_sum <- 1.5

# for reproducibility of the random resampling
set.seed(42)

# --- colors used for the comparison curves and comparison violin plots ---
cell_line_colors <- c(
  "HOXC10"       = "#2888c2",
  "HOXC10-13-10" = "#fd963a",
  "HOXC13"       = "#b81d19",
  "HOXC13-10-13" = "#8170b5",
  "H2B"          = "#4D4C4E"
)

# The ribbons on the comparison FRAP curves are mean +/- 1 SEM, where the
# SEM is calculated per frame across ALL individual ROIs from ALL
# replicates (replicates are not used for the ribbon, and the line is the
# mean of all ROIs, not the mean of replicate means).

# Folder where all PDF figures are exported (created if missing)
pdf_export_folder <- file.path(curve_folder, "pdf_figures")
dir.create(pdf_export_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## List and read individual-curve files

```{r list-and-read}
curve_files <- list.files(
  curve_folder,
  pattern    = "_individual_curves\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive  = recursive
)

curve_files

individual_curves <- curve_files %>%
  map_dfr(read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  # replicate + roi_id uniquely identifies one region's curve across every
  # replicate/file that got combined into curve_folder
  mutate(curve_id = paste(replicate, roi_id, sep = " | "))

head(individual_curves)
```

## Total number of individual curves

```{r count-curves}
curve_counts <- individual_curves %>%
  distinct(cell_line, channel, curve_id) %>%
  count(cell_line, channel, name = "n_curves")

curve_counts

total_curves_overall <- n_distinct(individual_curves$curve_id)
cat("Total individual curves across all cell lines, channels, and replicates:",
    total_curves_overall, "\n")
```

## Average curve across all individual curves, per cell line

Every individual region, from every file and every replicate, belonging
to a cell line is pooled together here - so a cell line with 40 curves
contributes all 40 to the average, regardless of how many replicates or
files they came from. Grouped by `cell_line`, `channel`, and `frame`.

```{r average-curve}
avg_curves <- individual_curves %>%
  filter(!is.na(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted)) %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel, frame) %>%
  summarize(
    time       = first(time),
    n_curves   = n(),
    mean_ratio = mean(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_ratio   = sd(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

head(avg_curves)
```

```{r plot-average-curves, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
for (cl in select_cell_lines(unique(avg_curves$cell_line))) {

  p <- avg_curves %>%
    filter(cell_line == cl) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = time, y = mean_ratio)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey70") +
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(ymin = mean_ratio - sd_ratio, ymax = mean_ratio + sd_ratio),
      alpha = 0.2, fill = "#2C7FB8"
    ) +
    geom_line(color = "#2C7FB8", linewidth = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ channel, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Cell line:", cl, "- average across all individual curves"),
      subtitle = "Mean ± SD, pooled across all regions and replicates",
      x = "Time (s)", y = "Targeted / Untargeted"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  if (!is.na(bleach_time)) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = bleach_time, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50")
  }

  print(p)
}
```

## Comparison plots of average curves (mean of all ROIs ± 1 SEM across all ROIs)

Four comparison figures, each exported as a PDF (one per channel in
`channels_to_model`) to `pdf_figures/average_curve_comparisons`:
HOXC10 vs HOXC13, H2B alone, HOXC10 vs HOXC10-13-10, and HOXC13 vs
HOXC13-10-13. The line is the mean over **all individual ROIs from all
replicates**, and the ribbon is ± 1 standard error of the mean across those
same ROIs (replicates are not used for the ribbon). These plots ignore
`cell_lines_to_plot`.

```{r plot-comparison-curves, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
curve_comparisons <- list(
  "HOXC10_vs_HOXC13"       = c("HOXC10", "HOXC13"),
  "H2B"                    = c("H2B"),
  "HOXC10_vs_HOXC10-13-10" = c("HOXC10", "HOXC10-13-10"),
  "HOXC13_vs_HOXC13-10-13" = c("HOXC13", "HOXC13-10-13")
)

roi_summary_curves <- individual_curves %>%
  filter(!is.na(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted)) %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel, frame) %>%
  summarize(
    time       = first(time),
    n_rois     = n(),
    mean_ratio = mean(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted),
    sd_ratio   = sd(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sem_ratio = sd_ratio / sqrt(n_rois),
    ci_lower  = mean_ratio - sem_ratio,
    ci_upper  = mean_ratio + sem_ratio
  )

curve_pdf_folder <- file.path(pdf_export_folder, "average_curve_comparisons")
dir.create(curve_pdf_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

for (ch in channels_to_model) {
  for (nm in names(curve_comparisons)) {

    lines_here <- curve_comparisons[[nm]]

    labels_df <- curve_counts %>%
      filter(channel == ch, cell_line %in% lines_here) %>%
      mutate(label = paste0(cell_line, " (n = ", n_curves, " ROIs)"))

    if (nrow(labels_df) == 0) {
      message(sprintf("No data for %s, channel '%s' - skipping comparison plot.",
                      paste(lines_here, collapse = " / "), ch))
      next
    }

    d <- roi_summary_curves %>%
      filter(channel == ch, cell_line %in% lines_here) %>%
      left_join(labels_df %>% select(cell_line, label), by = "cell_line")

    label_colors <- setNames(cell_line_colors[labels_df$cell_line], labels_df$label)

    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = time, y = mean_ratio, color = label, fill = label)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey70") +
      geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), alpha = 0.25, color = NA) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
      scale_color_manual(values = label_colors) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = label_colors) +
      labs(
        title = paste0(paste(lines_here, collapse = " vs. "), " - channel: ", ch),
        subtitle = "Mean of all ROIs from all replicates; ribbon = ± 1 SEM across ROIs",
        x = "Time (s)", y = "Targeted / Untargeted", color = NULL, fill = NULL
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")

    if (!is.na(bleach_time)) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = bleach_time, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50")
    }

    print(p)

    ggsave(
      file.path(curve_pdf_folder, paste0(nm, "_", ch, ".pdf")),
      p, width = 7, height = 5, device = "pdf"
    )
  }
}
```

## Model the average recovery curves (mono-, bi-, tri-exponential)

Fits each average cell-line/channel curve (restricted to
`channels_to_model`) with one, two, or three exponential terms:

$$y = C + A_1(1-e^{-k_1 t}) \;[+ A_2(1-e^{-k_2 t})] \;[+ A_3(1-e^{-k_3 t})]$$

`C` is the offset (value at the bleach frame), each `A_i` is the amplitude
of a recovery component, and each `k_i` its rate constant (time constant
tau_i = 1/k_i). Fits use `minpack.lm::nlsLM()` with non-negative bounds on
all parameters for physically sensible results.

**Only the post-bleach recovery phase is fit.** A sum of terms like
`1 - exp(-k*t)` is monotonically increasing, so it can only ever describe
a curve that rises smoothly to a plateau. So for each curve, the code
finds the bleach frame (from `bleach_time`, fixed or auto-detected), then
fits only the data from that point onward, with time re-zeroed so `t = 0`
at the bleach frame.

**Each fit is wrapped in `tryCatch()`**, so if a particular cell
line/channel/model combination fails to converge, it's recorded with an
error message and the loop moves on. Fits are also skipped (with a
message) if there aren't enough post-bleach data points to support the
number of free parameters in that model.

```{r fit-params}
# Which exponential model orders to try for each curve (1 = mono, 2 = bi, 3 = tri)
exp_orders_to_try <- c(1, 2, 3)

# Minimum number of post-bleach data points required, over and above the
# number of free parameters in the model, before a fit is even attempted.
min_extra_points <- 3
```

```{r fit-helpers}
# The bleach frame for a curve: the fixed `bleach_time` from the Parameters
# section if set, otherwise auto-detected as the time of the minimum
# mean_ratio (the bleach dip is normally the lowest point in the curve).
get_bleach_time <- function(time, y) {
  if (!is.na(bleach_time)) return(bleach_time)
  time[which.min(y)]
}

# Builds the recovery formula for a given number of exponential terms, e.g.
# for n_exp = 2: y ~ C + A1 * (1 - exp(-k1 * t)) + A2 * (1 - exp(-k2 * t))
build_exp_formula <- function(n_exp) {
  terms <- paste0("A", 1:n_exp, " * (1 - exp(-k", 1:n_exp, " * t))")
  as.formula(paste("y ~ C +", paste(terms, collapse = " + ")))
}

# Rough starting values: offset at the first observed value, amplitude split
# evenly across the terms, and rate constants spread across fast/medium/slow
# relative to the time span of the curve.
guess_start_params <- function(t, y, n_exp) {
  y0      <- y[which.min(t)]
  plateau <- mean(tail(y[order(t)], max(3, round(length(y) * 0.1))))
  amp_total <- max(plateau - y0, 1e-3)

  t_span <- diff(range(t))
  if (!is.finite(t_span) || t_span <= 0) t_span <- 1

  fracs <- list(`1` = 0.3, `2` = c(0.15, 0.5), `3` = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7))[[as.character(n_exp)]]
  ks    <- 1 / (t_span * fracs)

  start <- c(C = max(y0, 0))
  for (i in seq_len(n_exp)) {
    start[paste0("A", i)] <- amp_total / n_exp
    start[paste0("k", i)] <- ks[i]
  }
  start
}

# Fits one exponential model to one curve. Never throws an error itself -
# always returns a list with $fit = NULL and a readable $error message if
# the fit didn't work, so callers can just check `is.null(res$fit)`.
fit_recovery_model <- function(t, y, n_exp) {
  form  <- build_exp_formula(n_exp)
  start <- guess_start_params(t, y, n_exp)
  lower <- rep(0, length(start))
  names(lower) <- names(start)
  dat   <- data.frame(t = t, y = y)

  tryCatch({
    fit <- minpack.lm::nlsLM(
      form, data = dat, start = as.list(start), lower = lower,
      control = minpack.lm::nls.lm.control(maxiter = 500)
    )
    list(fit = fit, error = NA_character_)
  }, error = function(e) {
    list(fit = NULL, error = conditionMessage(e))
  })
}

# Multi-exponential fits are only identified up to a permutation of the
# (A_i, k_i) pairs - nlsLM() has no notion of "fast" vs "slow" component,
# so which pair ends up labeled A1/k1 vs A2/k2 (etc.) is really just an
# artifact of the starting values in guess_start_params(). This re-sorts a
# fitted coefficient vector so k1 is always the fastest (largest) rate
# constant, down to k_n the slowest, moving each A_i along with its paired
# k_i so amplitude/rate pairs stay matched. C is left untouched. Applied
# right after coef(fit) everywhere a model is fit, so "k1"/"A1" always mean
# the same thing (fastest component) in fit_results and in every bootstrap
# iteration.
sort_components_by_rate <- function(co, n_exp) {
  if (n_exp <= 1) return(co)

  k_names <- paste0("k", seq_len(n_exp))
  ord     <- order(co[k_names], decreasing = TRUE)

  sorted <- co
  for (i in seq_len(n_exp)) {
    sorted[paste0("A", i)] <- co[paste0("A", ord[i])]
    sorted[paste0("k", i)] <- co[paste0("k", ord[i])]
  }
  sorted
}
```

```{r run-fits}
fit_data <- avg_curves %>% filter(channel %in% channels_to_model)

fit_combinations <- fit_data %>% distinct(cell_line, channel)

model_labels <- c(`1` = "mono-exponential", `2` = "bi-exponential", `3` = "tri-exponential")

fit_results_list     <- list()
fit_predictions_list <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(fit_combinations))) {
  cl <- fit_combinations$cell_line[i]
  ch <- fit_combinations$channel[i]

  curve_full <- fit_data %>%
    filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch) %>%
    arrange(time)

  t0 <- get_bleach_time(curve_full$time, curve_full$mean_ratio)

  curve_data <- curve_full %>%
    filter(time >= t0) %>%
    mutate(t_fit = time - t0)

  for (n_exp in exp_orders_to_try) {

    model_label <- unname(model_labels[as.character(n_exp)])
    n_params    <- 2 * n_exp + 1
    min_points  <- n_params + min_extra_points

    if (nrow(curve_data) < min_points) {
      err_msg <- sprintf(
        "only %d post-bleach point(s) available, need at least %d for a %d-parameter model",
        nrow(curve_data), min_points, n_params
      )
      message(sprintf(
        "Fit skipped for cell line '%s', channel '%s', %s: %s",
        cl, ch, model_label, err_msg
      ))

      fit_results_list[[length(fit_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
        cell_line = cl, channel = ch, model = model_label, n_exp = n_exp,
        converged = FALSE, error = err_msg,
        bleach_time_used = t0, n_points_fit = nrow(curve_data),
        AIC = NA_real_, BIC = NA_real_, RSE = NA_real_
      )
      next
    }

    res <- fit_recovery_model(curve_data$t_fit, curve_data$mean_ratio, n_exp)

    if (is.null(res$fit)) {
      message(sprintf(
        "Fit failed for cell line '%s', channel '%s', %s: %s",
        cl, ch, model_label, res$error
      ))

      fit_results_list[[length(fit_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
        cell_line = cl, channel = ch, model = model_label, n_exp = n_exp,
        converged = FALSE, error = res$error,
        bleach_time_used = t0, n_points_fit = nrow(curve_data),
        AIC = NA_real_, BIC = NA_real_, RSE = NA_real_
      )
      next
    }

    fit <- res$fit
    co  <- coef(fit)
    co  <- sort_components_by_rate(co, n_exp)

    k_vals   <- co[grepl("^k", names(co))]
    tau_vals <- 1 / k_vals
    names(tau_vals) <- paste0("tau_", seq_along(tau_vals))

    params_row <- as_tibble(as.list(co)) %>%
      bind_cols(as_tibble(as.list(tau_vals)))

    fit_results_list[[length(fit_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
      cell_line = cl, channel = ch, model = model_label, n_exp = n_exp,
      converged = TRUE, error = NA_character_,
      bleach_time_used = t0, n_points_fit = nrow(curve_data),
      AIC = AIC(fit), BIC = BIC(fit), RSE = summary(fit)$sigma
    ) %>%
      bind_cols(params_row)

    fitted_vals <- predict(fit)

    fit_predictions_list[[length(fit_predictions_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
      cell_line = cl, channel = ch, model = model_label, n_exp = n_exp,
      time = curve_data$time, observed = curve_data$mean_ratio,
      fitted = fitted_vals, residual = curve_data$mean_ratio - fitted_vals
    )
  }
}

fit_results     <- bind_rows(fit_results_list)
fit_predictions <- bind_rows(fit_predictions_list)

# Mobile fraction = total recovered amplitude / (1 - offset), assuming the
# pre-bleach baseline is normalized to 1. Immobile fraction is the
# complement. Both are only computed for converged fits.
fit_results <- fit_results %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    mobile_fraction = if (converged) {
      sum(c_across(matches("^A[0-9]+$")), na.rm = TRUE) / (1 - C)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    immobile_fraction = if (converged) 1 - mobile_fraction else NA_real_,
    # unrecovered_raw: 1 - C - sum(A_i) - the raw, un-normalized gap
    # between the pre-bleach baseline and the fitted plateau ("what
    # percentage does not recover", with no division at all). An
    # alternative to immobile_fraction for plots where you want to read
    # the un-recovered amount directly, without normalizing for how deep
    # the bleach itself went.
    unrecovered_raw = if (converged) {
      1 - C - sum(c_across(matches("^A[0-9]+$")), na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Each component's own amplitude, and unrecovered_raw, expressed as a
  # share of the recoverable range (divided by 1 - C). frac_unrecovered is
  # mathematically identical to immobile_fraction; it's computed
  # separately here so it sits alongside frac_A1/frac_A2/... as one
  # self-contained "divided by 1 - C" group of columns. across() only
  # touches whichever A_i columns actually exist, so this works for
  # mono-, bi-, or tri-exponential fits without any special-casing.
  mutate(
    across(matches("^A[0-9]+$"), ~ .x / (1 - C), .names = "frac_{.col}"),
    frac_unrecovered = unrecovered_raw / (1 - C)
  )

fit_results
```

## Best-fitting model per curve

Among the models that converged, picks the one with the lowest AIC for
each cell line/channel. This is the model order used below, both for
display and as the model fit during the bootstrap.

```{r best-fits-table}
best_fits <- fit_results %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel) %>%
  slice_min(AIC, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

best_fits
```

## Plot: average curves with fitted recovery curves overlaid

One plot per cell line per model order (faceted by channel).

```{r plot-fits, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
for (model_lbl in unname(model_labels)) {

  preds_model <- fit_predictions %>% filter(model == model_lbl)

  for (cl in select_cell_lines(unique(fit_data$cell_line))) {

    obs   <- fit_data %>% filter(cell_line == cl)
    preds <- preds_model %>% filter(cell_line == cl)
    bleach_ref <- fit_results %>%
      filter(cell_line == cl, model == model_lbl) %>%
      distinct(channel, bleach_time_used)

    p <- ggplot() +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey70") +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = obs,
        aes(x = time, ymin = mean_ratio - sd_ratio, ymax = mean_ratio + sd_ratio),
        alpha = 0.15, fill = "grey50"
      ) +
      geom_point(data = obs, aes(x = time, y = mean_ratio), color = "grey30", size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6)

    if (nrow(bleach_ref) > 0) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(
        data = bleach_ref, aes(xintercept = bleach_time_used),
        linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50"
      )
    }

    if (nrow(preds) > 0) {
      p <- p + geom_line(data = preds, aes(x = time, y = fitted), color = "#D95F02", linewidth = 1)
    }

    p <- p +
      facet_wrap(~ channel, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(
        title = paste("Cell line:", cl, "-", model_lbl, "fit"),
        x = "Time (s)", y = "Targeted / Untargeted"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()

    print(p)
  }
}
```

## Plot: fit residuals


## Alternative: per-replicate fits

As an alternative to the resampling-based bootstrap below, this fits each
**replicate's own average curve independently**: every individual curve
belonging to one replicate is averaged into that replicate's average
curve, and that curve is fit on its own using `bootstrap_model` (the same
model used for the bootstrap, so the two approaches are directly
comparable). Across the resulting per-replicate fits, each parameter's
**mean and SD across replicates** is reported - an estimate of
variability driven by real replicate-to-replicate differences, rather
than by resampling the same pooled pool of curves. As with `fit_results`
above, rate constants are reported as `tau_i = 1/k_i`, not as a
half-time.

A given cell line/channel is only fit if `bootstrap_model` actually
converged on the pooled average curve there (same requirement as the
bootstrap uses to pick `n_exp`); within that, an individual replicate is
skipped (and listed in the failed-fits table below) if it doesn't have
enough post-bleach points or its own fit doesn't converge.

```{r replicate-average-curves}
replicate_avg_curves <- individual_curves %>%
  filter(!is.na(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted)) %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel, replicate, frame) %>%
  summarize(
    time       = first(time),
    n_curves   = n(),
    mean_ratio = mean(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

head(replicate_avg_curves)
```

```{r replicate-fits}
replicate_fit_results_list     <- list()
replicate_fit_predictions_list <- list()

for (cl in unique(replicate_avg_curves$cell_line)) {

  channels_here <- intersect(
    channels_to_model,
    unique(replicate_avg_curves$channel[replicate_avg_curves$cell_line == cl])
  )

  for (ch in channels_here) {

    # use the same model order chosen for the bootstrap, and require that
    # it actually converged on the pooled average curve for this cell
    # line/channel - same requirement the bootstrap uses above
    chosen_row <- fit_results %>%
      filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch, model == bootstrap_model, converged)

    if (nrow(chosen_row) == 0) {
      message(sprintf(
        "No converged '%s' fit found for cell line '%s', channel '%s' - skipping per-replicate fits.",
        bootstrap_model, cl, ch
      ))
      next
    }

    n_exp <- chosen_row$n_exp[1]

    replicates_here <- replicate_avg_curves %>%
      filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch) %>%
      pull(replicate) %>%
      unique()

    for (rep in replicates_here) {

      curve_full <- replicate_avg_curves %>%
        filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch, replicate == rep) %>%
        arrange(time)

      t0 <- get_bleach_time(curve_full$time, curve_full$mean_ratio)

      curve_data <- curve_full %>%
        filter(time >= t0) %>%
        mutate(t_fit = time - t0)

      n_params   <- 2 * n_exp + 1
      min_points <- n_params + min_extra_points

      if (nrow(curve_data) < min_points) {
        replicate_fit_results_list[[length(replicate_fit_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
          cell_line = cl, channel = ch, replicate = rep, model = bootstrap_model, n_exp = n_exp,
          converged = FALSE, error = "too few post-bleach points",
          bleach_time_used = t0, n_points_fit = nrow(curve_data)
        )
        next
      }

      res <- fit_recovery_model(curve_data$t_fit, curve_data$mean_ratio, n_exp)

      if (is.null(res$fit)) {
        replicate_fit_results_list[[length(replicate_fit_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
          cell_line = cl, channel = ch, replicate = rep, model = bootstrap_model, n_exp = n_exp,
          converged = FALSE, error = res$error,
          bleach_time_used = t0, n_points_fit = nrow(curve_data)
        )
        next
      }

      fit <- res$fit
      co  <- coef(fit)
      co  <- sort_components_by_rate(co, n_exp)

      k_vals   <- co[grepl("^k", names(co))]
      tau_vals <- 1 / k_vals
      names(tau_vals) <- paste0("tau_", seq_along(tau_vals))

      mobile_fraction   <- unname(sum(co[grepl("^A", names(co))]) / (1 - co["C"]))
      immobile_fraction <- 1 - mobile_fraction

      params_row <- as_tibble(as.list(co)) %>%
        bind_cols(as_tibble(as.list(tau_vals)))

      replicate_fit_results_list[[length(replicate_fit_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
        cell_line = cl, channel = ch, replicate = rep, model = bootstrap_model, n_exp = n_exp,
        converged = TRUE, error = NA_character_,
        bleach_time_used = t0, n_points_fit = nrow(curve_data),
        mobile_fraction = mobile_fraction, immobile_fraction = immobile_fraction
      ) %>%
        bind_cols(params_row)

      fitted_vals <- predict(fit)

      replicate_fit_predictions_list[[length(replicate_fit_predictions_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
        cell_line = cl, channel = ch, replicate = rep, model = bootstrap_model, n_exp = n_exp,
        time = curve_data$time, observed = curve_data$mean_ratio,
        fitted = fitted_vals, residual = curve_data$mean_ratio - fitted_vals
      )
    }
  }
}

replicate_fit_results     <- bind_rows(replicate_fit_results_list)
replicate_fit_predictions <- bind_rows(replicate_fit_predictions_list)

# Same unrecovered_raw / frac_A* / frac_unrecovered columns as fit_results
# above (see the comments there) - added once, vectorized, on the full
# bound table rather than inside the loop.
replicate_fit_results <- replicate_fit_results %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    unrecovered_raw = if (converged) {
      1 - C - sum(c_across(matches("^A[0-9]+$")), na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    across(matches("^A[0-9]+$"), ~ .x / (1 - C), .names = "frac_{.col}"),
    frac_unrecovered = unrecovered_raw / (1 - C)
  )

replicate_fit_results
```

```{r replicate-fits-failed}
replicate_failed <- replicate_fit_results %>% filter(!converged)

if (nrow(replicate_failed) > 0) {
  replicate_failed %>%
    select(cell_line, channel, replicate, model, bleach_time_used, n_points_fit, error) %>%
    knitr::kable()
} else {
  cat("All per-replicate fits converged.")
}
```

### Plot: each replicate's average curve with its own fit overlaid

Before summarizing across replicates, this shows every replicate's fit
individually - one panel per channel/replicate combination - so you can
see directly how much the fitted curve (and not just the extracted
parameters) actually varies from replicate to replicate.

```{r plot-replicate-fits, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
for (cl in select_cell_lines(unique(replicate_avg_curves$cell_line))) {

  obs   <- replicate_avg_curves %>% filter(cell_line == cl, channel %in% channels_to_model)
  preds <- replicate_fit_predictions %>% filter(cell_line == cl)

  if (nrow(preds) == 0) next

  bleach_ref <- replicate_fit_results %>%
    filter(cell_line == cl, converged) %>%
    distinct(channel, replicate, bleach_time_used)

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey70") +
    geom_point(data = obs, aes(x = time, y = mean_ratio), color = "grey30", size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6)

  if (nrow(bleach_ref) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(
      data = bleach_ref, aes(xintercept = bleach_time_used),
      linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50"
    )
  }

  p <- p +
    geom_line(data = preds, aes(x = time, y = fitted), color = "#D95F02", linewidth = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ channel + replicate, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Cell line: ", cl, " - per-replicate ", bootstrap_model, " fits"),
      x = "Time (s)", y = "Targeted / Untargeted"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p)
}
```

### Per-replicate fit parameter summary (mean ± SD across replicates)

```{r replicate-fits-summary}
replicate_param_cols <- replicate_fit_results %>%
  select(matches("^C$"), matches("^A[0-9]+$"), matches("^k[0-9]+$"),
         matches("^tau_[0-9]+$"), unrecovered_raw) %>%
  names()

replicate_counts <- replicate_avg_curves %>%
  distinct(cell_line, channel, replicate) %>%
  count(cell_line, channel, name = "n_replicates_total")

replicate_fit_summary <- replicate_fit_results %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel) %>%
  summarize(
    n_replicates_converged = n(),
    across(
      all_of(replicate_param_cols),
      list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(replicate_counts, by = c("cell_line", "channel")) %>%
  relocate(n_replicates_total, .after = channel)

replicate_fit_summary %>% knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

```{r plot-replicate-fits-summary, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
replicate_fit_summary_long <- replicate_fit_summary %>%
  select(cell_line, channel, ends_with("_mean"), ends_with("_sd")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(cell_line, channel),
    names_to = c("parameter", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(mean|sd)$"
  )

# one row per replicate per parameter, so each replicate's own fitted value
# can be overlaid as a dot on top of the mean ± SD bar
replicate_fit_points <- replicate_fit_results %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  select(cell_line, channel, replicate, all_of(replicate_param_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(replicate_param_cols), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value")

# one fixed point shape per replicate (shared across all cell lines/
# channels/parameters below, so e.g. "replicate 1" is always the same
# shape everywhere), rather than color, since color is already used for
# the bars.
replicate_levels <- sort(unique(replicate_fit_points$replicate))
replicate_shape_values <- setNames(rep(0:25, length.out = length(replicate_levels)), replicate_levels)

for (ch in unique(replicate_fit_summary_long$channel)) {

  stat   <- replicate_fit_summary_long %>% filter(channel == ch, cell_line %in% select_cell_lines(unique(replicate_fit_summary_long$cell_line)))
  points <- replicate_fit_points %>% filter(channel == ch, cell_line %in% select_cell_lines(unique(replicate_fit_points$cell_line)))

  p <- ggplot(stat, aes(x = cell_line, y = mean, fill = cell_line)) +
    geom_col(alpha = 0.6, width = 0.7) +

      aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
      width = 0.25, color = "#D95F02", linewidth = 0.8
    ) +

      inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.12, height = 0,

    ) +

      subtitle = "Bar = mean across replicate average-curve fits; error bar = ± 1 SD; dot shape = replicate",
      x = "Cell line", y = "Value", shape = "Replicate"
    ) +

    guides(fill = "none")

  print(p)
}
```

### Per-replicate: A_i and unrecovered fraction, each divided by (1 - C)

A second view of the same per-replicate fits, decomposing the recoverable
range (`1 - C`) into each component's own share (`A_i / (1 - C)`) plus the
share that never recovered (`frac_unrecovered`, i.e. `unrecovered_raw /
(1 - C)`) - together these sum to 1 for a given replicate. Kept separate
from the panel above so it isn't mixed in with `C`, `k_i`, and `tau_i` on
very different scales. Works for mono-, bi-, or tri-exponential fits
without changes, since it only plots whichever `frac_A*` columns exist.

```{r plot-replicate-fits-fractions, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
replicate_fraction_points <- replicate_fit_results %>%

for (ch in unique(replicate_fraction_summary_long$channel)) {
```

## Bootstrap resampling of individual curves (all cell lines)

For every cell line found in the data, and separately for each channel in
`channels_to_model`, this repeats the following `n_bootstrap_iterations`
(1,000) times:

1. Let `x` = the number of individual curves actually available for this
   cell line/channel (from `curve_counts` above).
2. Randomly draw `x` curves **with replacement** from that pool - so the
   same individual curve can be picked more than once in a given
   iteration, and left out entirely in another.
3. Average the drawn curves (duplicates included, so a curve picked twice
   counts twice toward the average) into one resampled recovery curve.
4. Re-fit that resampled curve using `bootstrap_model` (set manually in
   the Parameters section, default `"bi-exponential"` - independent of
   whatever `best_fits` picked by AIC above). The chosen model must have
   actually converged on the full average curve (i.e. have a row in
   `fit_results`) for a given cell line/channel, or that channel is
   skipped with a message. An iteration whose fit converges but whose
   plateau (`C + sum(A_i)`) exceeds `max_plateau_sum`, or in which any rate
   constant `k_i` lands exactly on its lower bound of 0 (making
   `tau_i = 1/k_i` infinite), is discarded rather than saved (see
   "Bootstrap discard summary" below).

After 1,000 iterations, the saved parameters are summarized as a mean and
SD per parameter, which reflects how much the fit would plausibly vary if
you'd happened to image a different random subset of regions.

Curves are drawn separately per cell line and per channel, since each
cell line/channel combination has its own curve pool and its own average
curve/fit.

```{r bootstrap-helper}
# Builds one resampled "average" curve from an already-drawn vector of
# curve_ids (which may contain repeats, since draws are made with
# replacement): each draw's curve contributes its full time series again,
# and the ratio is averaged across all draws at each frame.
build_resampled_curve <- function(curve_frame_data, sampled_ids) {
  sample_draws <- tibble(draw = seq_along(sampled_ids), curve_id = sampled_ids)

  sample_draws %>%
    left_join(curve_frame_data, by = "curve_id", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    group_by(frame) %>%
    summarize(
      time       = first(time),
      mean_ratio = mean(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups    = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r bootstrap-run}
bootstrap_results_list <- list()

for (cl in unique(curve_counts$cell_line)) {

  bootstrap_pool <- individual_curves %>%
    filter(cell_line == cl,
           channel %in% channels_to_model,
           !is.na(ratio_targeted_to_untargeted))

  for (ch in intersect(channels_to_model, unique(bootstrap_pool$channel))) {

    curve_frame_data <- bootstrap_pool %>%
      filter(channel == ch) %>%
      select(curve_id, frame, time, ratio_targeted_to_untargeted)

    curve_pool <- unique(curve_frame_data$curve_id)
    n_draw     <- length(curve_pool)

    # look up the manually chosen model, requiring that it actually
    # converged on the full average curve for this cell line/channel
    chosen_row <- fit_results %>%
      filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch,
             model == bootstrap_model, converged)

    if (nrow(chosen_row) == 0 || n_draw == 0) {
      message(sprintf(
        "No converged '%s' fit (or no curves) found for cell line '%s', channel '%s' - skipping bootstrap.",
        bootstrap_model, cl, ch
      ))
      next
    }

    n_exp       <- chosen_row$n_exp[1]
    model_label <- bootstrap_model

    message(sprintf(
      "Bootstrapping cell line '%s', channel '%s': %d curves available, drawing %d per iteration (with replacement), %s model, %d iterations...",
      cl, ch, n_draw, n_draw, model_label, n_bootstrap_iterations
    ))

    for (iter in seq_len(n_bootstrap_iterations)) {

      # draw first, so we can track how many *distinct* curves ended up in
      # this iteration's sample (repeats are expected, since draws are with
      # replacement)
      sampled_ids     <- sample(curve_pool, size = n_draw, replace = TRUE)
      n_unique_curves <- length(unique(sampled_ids))

      resampled_curve <- build_resampled_curve(curve_frame_data, sampled_ids)

      t0 <- get_bleach_time(resampled_curve$time, resampled_curve$mean_ratio)

      fit_data_iter <- resampled_curve %>%
        filter(time >= t0) %>%
        mutate(t_fit = time - t0)

      n_params   <- 2 * n_exp + 1
      min_points <- n_params + min_extra_points

      if (nrow(fit_data_iter) < min_points) {
        bootstrap_results_list[[length(bootstrap_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
          cell_line = cl, channel = ch, iteration = iter,
          n_curves_drawn = n_draw, n_unique_curves = n_unique_curves,
          converged = FALSE, error = "too few post-bleach points",
          discard_reason = "fit_failed"
        )
        next
      }

      res <- fit_recovery_model(fit_data_iter$t_fit, fit_data_iter$mean_ratio, n_exp)

      if (is.null(res$fit)) {
        bootstrap_results_list[[length(bootstrap_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
          cell_line = cl, channel = ch, iteration = iter,
          n_curves_drawn = n_draw, n_unique_curves = n_unique_curves,
          converged = FALSE, error = res$error,
          discard_reason = "fit_failed"
        )
        next
      }

      fit <- res$fit
      co  <- coef(fit)
      co  <- sort_components_by_rate(co, n_exp)

      # discard iterations whose fitted plateau (C + sum of all A_i) is
      # implausibly high - see max_plateau_sum in the Parameters section
      plateau_sum <- unname(co["C"] + sum(co[grepl("^A", names(co))]))

      if (plateau_sum > max_plateau_sum) {
        bootstrap_results_list[[length(bootstrap_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
          cell_line = cl, channel = ch, iteration = iter,
          n_curves_drawn = n_draw, n_unique_curves = n_unique_curves,
          converged = FALSE,
          error = sprintf("discarded: C + sum(A_i) = %.3f exceeds max_plateau_sum (%.2f)",
                           plateau_sum, max_plateau_sum),
          discard_reason = "plateau_too_high"
        )
        next
      }

      # discard iterations where any rate constant landed exactly on its
      # lower bound (0) in fit_recovery_model(). k_i = 0 is itself a
      # legitimate fit result (that component doesn't move on an
      # observable timescale in this iteration's resampled curve), but
      # tau_i = 1/k_i is then Inf, and a single Inf poisons every
      # downstream mean/SD - and, if this happens often enough for a given
      # cell line/channel, even the median - computed across iterations
      # for that tau_i column. Since k_i can't go below 0 (it's
      # box-constrained there), k_i <= 0 here can only mean it sits
      # exactly on the boundary, not floating-point noise. The whole
      # iteration is discarded (not just tau_i) - a component that
      # vanished this way makes every parameter's estimate for this
      # iteration suspect, not only the rate that hit the wall.
      k_vals <- co[grepl("^k", names(co))]

      if (any(k_vals <= 0)) {
        bootstrap_results_list[[length(bootstrap_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
          cell_line = cl, channel = ch, iteration = iter,
          n_curves_drawn = n_draw, n_unique_curves = n_unique_curves,
          converged = FALSE,
          error = sprintf("discarded: rate constant(s) %s landed on the lower bound (0) - tau undefined",
                           paste(names(k_vals)[k_vals <= 0], collapse = ", ")),
          discard_reason = "rate_at_lower_bound"
        )
        next
      }

      tau_vals <- 1 / k_vals
      names(tau_vals) <- paste0("tau_", seq_along(tau_vals))

      mobile_fraction   <- unname(sum(co[grepl("^A", names(co))]) / (1 - co["C"]))
      immobile_fraction <- 1 - mobile_fraction

      params_row <- as_tibble(as.list(co)) %>%
        bind_cols(as_tibble(as.list(tau_vals)))

      bootstrap_results_list[[length(bootstrap_results_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
        cell_line = cl, channel = ch, iteration = iter,
        n_curves_drawn = n_draw, n_unique_curves = n_unique_curves,
        converged = TRUE, error = NA_character_, discard_reason = NA_character_,
        mobile_fraction = mobile_fraction, immobile_fraction = immobile_fraction
      ) %>%
        bind_cols(params_row)
    }
  }
}

bootstrap_params <- bind_rows(bootstrap_results_list)

# Same unrecovered_raw / frac_A* / frac_unrecovered columns as fit_results
# and replicate_fit_results above (see the comments there) - added once,
# vectorized, on the full bound table rather than inside the loop (much
# cheaper than computing it per-iteration for n_bootstrap_iterations rows).
bootstrap_params <- bootstrap_params %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    unrecovered_raw = if (converged) {
      1 - C - sum(c_across(matches("^A[0-9]+$")), na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    across(matches("^A[0-9]+$"), ~ .x / (1 - C), .names = "frac_{.col}"),
    frac_unrecovered = unrecovered_raw / (1 - C)
  )

head(bootstrap_params)
```

### Bootstrap discard summary

Every iteration lands in one of four buckets: **kept** (converged, its
plateau is within `max_plateau_sum`, and every rate constant is strictly
above its lower bound), **fit failed** (too few post-bleach points, or
`nlsLM()` itself didn't converge), **discarded - plateau too high**
(`nlsLM()` converged, but `C + sum(A_i)` exceeded `max_plateau_sum` and was
thrown out as a degenerate fit), or **discarded - rate at lower bound**
(`nlsLM()` converged, but at least one `k_i` landed exactly on its lower
bound of 0, making `tau_i = 1/k_i` infinite and unusable in any downstream
mean/SD/median). This reports what percentage of each cell line/channel's
iterations fell into each bucket.

```{r bootstrap-discard-summary}
bootstrap_discard_summary <- bootstrap_params %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel) %>%
  summarize(
    n_total               = n(),
    n_kept                = sum(converged),
    n_fit_failed          = sum(discard_reason == "fit_failed", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_high_plateau        = sum(discard_reason == "plateau_too_high", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_rate_at_boundary    = sum(discard_reason == "rate_at_lower_bound", na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_kept              = 100 * n_kept / n_total,
    pct_fit_failed        = 100 * n_fit_failed / n_total,
    pct_high_plateau      = 100 * n_high_plateau / n_total,
    pct_rate_at_boundary  = 100 * n_rate_at_boundary / n_total,
    pct_discarded_total   = 100 * (n_fit_failed + n_high_plateau + n_rate_at_boundary) / n_total,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bootstrap_discard_summary %>% knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

### Bootstrap parameter summary (median ± SD across 1,000 iterations)

```{r bootstrap-summary}
bootstrap_summary <- bootstrap_params %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel) %>%
  summarize(
    n_converged = n(),
    n_total     = n_bootstrap_iterations,
    across(
      c(matches("^C$"), matches("^A[0-9]+$"), matches("^k[0-9]+$"),
        matches("^tau_[0-9]+$"), mobile_fraction, immobile_fraction),
      list(median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bootstrap_summary %>% knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

### Bootstrap vs. single best fit of the average curve

Compares the bootstrap's median ± SD for each parameter against the single
fit obtained by fitting `bootstrap_model` directly to the full,
un-resampled average curve (the same fit validated in `fit_results`
before the bootstrap ran) - i.e. "what you'd report from one fit to all
the pooled data" vs. "what the bootstrap says that estimate's uncertainty
actually looks like." `z_single_fit_vs_bootstrap` is how many bootstrap
SDs the single fit sits from the bootstrap median - values well outside
roughly ±2 suggest the single fit on the full average curve landed
somewhere the resampled curves don't often reach.

Instead of `mobile_fraction`/`immobile_fraction`, the plot below shows
`unrecovered_raw` (`1 - C - sum(A_i)`, with no division) alongside the
other fit parameters.

```{r bootstrap-vs-single-fit}
param_cols_all <- bootstrap_params %>%
  select(matches("^C$"), matches("^A[0-9]+$"), matches("^k[0-9]+$"),
         matches("^tau_[0-9]+$"), unrecovered_raw) %>%
  names()

bootstrap_param_stats <- bootstrap_params %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  select(cell_line, channel, all_of(param_cols_all)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(param_cols_all), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel, parameter) %>%
  summarize(
    bootstrap_median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    bootstrap_sd     = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

single_fit_params <- fit_results %>%
  filter(model == bootstrap_model, converged) %>%
  select(cell_line, channel, any_of(param_cols_all)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(cell_line, channel), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "single_fit_value")

bootstrap_vs_single_fit <- single_fit_params %>%
  inner_join(bootstrap_param_stats, by = c("cell_line", "channel", "parameter")) %>%
  mutate(
    diff                      = single_fit_value - bootstrap_median,
    z_single_fit_vs_bootstrap = diff / bootstrap_sd
  ) %>%
  arrange(cell_line, channel, parameter)

bootstrap_vs_single_fit %>% knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

```{r plot-bootstrap-vs-single-fit, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
for (ch in unique(bootstrap_vs_single_fit$channel)) {

  df <- bootstrap_vs_single_fit %>%
    filter(channel == ch, cell_line != "H2B",
           cell_line %in% select_cell_lines(unique(bootstrap_vs_single_fit$cell_line)))

  q <- ggplot(df, aes(x = cell_line, y = bootstrap_median, fill = cell_line)) +
    geom_col(alpha = 0.6, width = 0.7) +
    geom_point(
      aes(y = single_fit_value), shape = 23, size = 2.5,
      fill = "black", color = "black"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Channel: ", ch, " - bootstrap median ± SD vs. single average-curve fit"),
      subtitle = "Bar = bootstrap median; black diamond = single fit to the full average curve",
      x = "Cell line", y = "Value"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")

  print(q)

   p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = cell_line, y = bootstrap_median, fill = cell_line)) +
    geom_col(alpha = 0.6, width = 0.7) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = bootstrap_median - bootstrap_sd, ymax = bootstrap_median + bootstrap_sd),
      width = 0.25, color = "#D95F02", linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_point(
      aes(y = single_fit_value), shape = 23, size = 2.5,
      fill = "black", color = "black"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Channel: ", ch, " - bootstrap median ± SD vs. single average-curve fit"),
      subtitle = "Bar + orange error bar = bootstrap median ± 1 SD; black diamond = single fit to the full average curve",
      x = "Cell line", y = "Value"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")

  print(p)
}
```

### Bootstrap: distribution across iterations (violin plots) and significance tests

The bar plots above only show each parameter's bootstrap median ± SD. The
plots below show the **whole distribution** of the bootstrap values for
each parameter as a violin plot on a **linear y-axis**, one violin per cell line, using
the same cell lines as the corresponding bar plot. A single horizontal
line inside each violin marks its median; no boxplot is drawn. All finite
values, including zero and negative values, are shown where present.

**Significance test.** For every parameter, every pair of plotted cell
lines is compared with a **bootstrap difference test**. Because each cell
line is resampled independently, pairing every iteration of cell line A
with every iteration of cell line B gives the bootstrap distribution of
the difference `A - B`. The two-sided p-value is
`2 * min(P(A > B), P(A < B))` (ties count half) - i.e. how often the
difference falls on the "wrong" side of zero, doubled. `prob_1_greater` in
the table is `P(group1 > group2)`: 0.5 means the two distributions fully
overlap, values near 0 or 1 mean they barely overlap. Two things to keep in
mind:

* Under each violin plot, a second set of plots shows the **distribution of
  the differences** `group1 - group2` behind each comparison (one figure per
  pair of cell lines, one panel per parameter), with a dashed line at 0.
  The p-value is the doubled share of the distribution on the smaller side
  of that line. The plotted differences are a random sample of 20,000
  pairings (the p-values and `prob_1_greater` use *all* pairings), and the
  x-axis shows the central 99% of that sample so a few extreme pairings
  don't squash the panels.
* The number of bootstrap iterations is arbitrary, so a plain
  Wilcoxon/t-test on the iterations would have p-values that shrink toward 0
  just by running more iterations; this test doesn't have that problem, but
  its resolution is limited to about `1 / n_iterations`, so p-values are
  floored there (shown as `<`).
* With more than two cell lines, p-values are Holm-adjusted across the
  pairwise comparisons within each parameter (`p_adj`). Stars on the plots
  are based on `p_adj`: `ns` p >= 0.05, `*` < 0.05, `**` < 0.01,
  `***` < 0.001.

```{r bootstrap-violin-helpers}
p_to_stars <- function(p) {
  case_when(is.na(p) ~ "NA", p < 0.001 ~ "***", p < 0.01 ~ "**", p < 0.05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "ns")
}

# Pairwise bootstrap difference test between cell lines, per parameter.
# `long_df` needs columns cell_line, parameter, value (one channel).
# P(A > B) over all pairings of A's and B's iterations equals the
# Mann-Whitney U statistic / (nA * nB), so it is computed from ranks
# instead of building the nA x nB matrix of differences.
bootstrap_pairwise_tests <- function(long_df) {
  # fewer than two cell lines -> nothing to compare (empty table, same columns)
  if (n_distinct(long_df$cell_line) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      parameter = character(), group1 = character(), group2 = character(),
      n1 = integer(), n2 = integer(), median1 = numeric(), median2 = numeric(),
      prob_1_greater = numeric(), p_raw = numeric(), p_floor = numeric(),
      p_is_floor = logical(), p_value = numeric(), p_adj = numeric(),
      significance = character(), p_adj_label = character()
    ))
  }

  long_df %>%
    group_by(parameter) %>%
    group_map(function(d, key) {
      lines <- sort(unique(d$cell_line))
      if (length(lines) < 2) return(NULL)

      map_dfr(combn(lines, 2, simplify = FALSE), function(pr) {
        a <- d$value[d$cell_line == pr[1]]; a <- a[is.finite(a)]
        b <- d$value[d$cell_line == pr[2]]; b <- b[is.finite(b)]
        na <- length(a); nb <- length(b)

        out <- tibble(
          parameter = key$parameter, group1 = pr[1], group2 = pr[2],
          n1 = na, n2 = nb,
          median1 = if (na > 0) median(a) else NA_real_,
          median2 = if (nb > 0) median(b) else NA_real_
        )

        if (na < 2 || nb < 2) {
          return(mutate(out, prob_1_greater = NA_real_, p_raw = NA_real_,
                        p_floor = NA_real_))
        }

        r    <- rank(c(a, b))
        u    <- sum(r[seq_len(na)]) - na * (na + 1) / 2
        prob <- u / (na * nb)

        mutate(out,
               prob_1_greater = prob,
               p_raw   = 2 * min(prob, 1 - prob),
               p_floor = 1 / min(na, nb))
      })
    }, .keep = TRUE) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    mutate(
      p_is_floor = !is.na(p_raw) & p_raw < p_floor,
      p_value    = pmax(p_raw, p_floor)
    ) %>%
    group_by(parameter) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "holm")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      significance = p_to_stars(p_adj),
      p_adj_label  = ifelse(is.na(p_adj), NA_character_,
                            paste0(ifelse(p_is_floor, "<", ""), sprintf("%.3g", p_adj)))
    )
}

# Violin plot on a linear y-axis for one channel, with a median line and
# significance brackets. Returns the plot, tests table, and pairwise differences.
bootstrap_violins_and_tests <- function(params_df, param_cols, ch, cell_lines, title, ylab,
                                        fill_values = NULL, keep_order = FALSE) {

  long <- params_df %>%
    filter(converged, channel == ch, cell_line %in% cell_lines) %>%
    select(cell_line, all_of(param_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = all_of(param_cols), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
    filter(is.finite(value))

  line_levels <- if (keep_order) intersect(cell_lines, unique(long$cell_line)) else sort(unique(long$cell_line))
  long <- long %>% mutate(cell_line = factor(cell_line, levels = line_levels))

  long_chr <- long %>% mutate(cell_line = as.character(cell_line))

  tests <- bootstrap_pairwise_tests(long_chr) %>%
    mutate(channel = ch, .before = 1)

  diffs <- bootstrap_pairwise_differences(long_chr)

  # Use all finite values; linear-axis plots can include zero and negatives.
  long_plot <- long

  # Significance brackets, stacked above each facet's highest violin value
  # using additive spacing for the linear y-axis.
  brackets <- tests %>%
    filter(!is.na(p_adj)) %>%
    inner_join(long_plot %>% group_by(parameter) %>% summarize(y_top = max(value), .groups = "drop"),
               by = "parameter") %>%
    group_by(parameter) %>%
    mutate(
      j  = row_number(),
      x1 = match(group1, line_levels),
      x2 = match(group2, line_levels),
      y  = y_top + pmax(abs(y_top) * 0.08, 0.05) * j
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  p <- ggplot(long_plot, aes(x = cell_line, y = value, fill = cell_line)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.6, scale = "width", trim = TRUE, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.28,
                 fatten = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_segment(data = brackets, aes(x = x1, xend = x2, y = y, yend = y),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(data = brackets, aes(x = (x1 + x2) / 2, y = y, label = significance),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
    # Invisible points just to leave room above the top bracket
    geom_blank(data = brackets, aes(x = (x1 + x2) / 2,
                                    y = y + pmax(abs(y) * 0.05, 0.05)),
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
    # y axis of every panel goes down to (at least) 0
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = paste0("Violin = distribution of kept bootstrap iterations; black line = median; ",
                        "brackets = Holm-adjusted bootstrap difference test"),
      x = "Cell line", y = ylab
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")

  if (!is.null(fill_values)) p <- p + scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values)

  list(plot = p, tests = tests, diffs = diffs)
}

# Random sample of pairings of cell line A's and cell line B's iterations,
# returned as the differences A - B (group1 - group2), per parameter and pair.
# Only used for plotting - the p-values above use every pairing. The seed is
# fixed here so the same data always gives the same plotted sample.
bootstrap_pairwise_differences <- function(long_df, n_pairs = 20000) {
  set.seed(123)

  long_df %>%
    group_by(parameter) %>%
    group_map(function(d, key) {
      lines <- sort(unique(d$cell_line))
      if (length(lines) < 2) return(NULL)

      map_dfr(combn(lines, 2, simplify = FALSE), function(pr) {
        a <- d$value[d$cell_line == pr[1]]; a <- a[is.finite(a)]
        b <- d$value[d$cell_line == pr[2]]; b <- b[is.finite(b)]
        if (length(a) < 2 || length(b) < 2) return(NULL)

        tibble(
          parameter = key$parameter, group1 = pr[1], group2 = pr[2],
          diff = a[sample.int(length(a), n_pairs, replace = TRUE)] -
                 b[sample.int(length(b), n_pairs, replace = TRUE)]
        )
      })
    }, .keep = TRUE) %>%
    bind_rows()
}

# One figure per pair of cell lines: histogram of group1 - group2 for every
# parameter (facets), coloured by which side of 0 each pairing falls on,
# dashed line at 0, and the test result written in the corner of each panel.
# Returns a list of ggplot objects.
plot_bootstrap_differences <- function(diffs, tests, ch) {
  if (nrow(diffs) == 0) return(list())

  comps <- diffs %>% distinct(group1, group2)

  map(seq_len(nrow(comps)), function(i) {
    g1 <- comps$group1[i]
    g2 <- comps$group2[i]
    lab_pos <- paste0(g1, " > ", g2)
    lab_neg <- paste0(g1, " < ", g2)

    d <- diffs %>%
      filter(group1 == g1, group2 == g2) %>%
      group_by(parameter) %>%
      filter(diff >= quantile(diff, 0.005), diff <= quantile(diff, 0.995)) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(side = factor(ifelse(diff > 0, lab_pos, lab_neg), levels = c(lab_pos, lab_neg)))

    ann <- tests %>%
      filter(group1 == g1, group2 == g2, !is.na(p_adj)) %>%
      mutate(label = sprintf("P(%s > %s) = %.3f\np_adj %s  %s",
                             g1, g2, prob_1_greater,
                             ifelse(p_is_floor, paste0("< ", sprintf("%.3g", p_adj)),
                                    paste0("= ", sprintf("%.3g", p_adj))),
                             significance))

    ggplot(d, aes(x = diff, fill = side)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 60, color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
      geom_text(data = ann, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
                hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.3, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(c("#D95F02", "#2C7FB8"), c(lab_pos, lab_neg))) +
      facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
      labs(
        title = paste0("Channel: ", ch, " - bootstrap differences: ", g1, " - ", g2),
        subtitle = paste0("Random sample of pairings of bootstrap iterations (central 99% shown); dashed line = 0 (no difference). ",
                          "Labels use all pairings."),
        x = paste0("Difference (", g1, " - ", g2, ")"), y = "Number of pairings", fill = NULL
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })
}

# collected across channels/plots, written out in the export chunk at the end
bootstrap_violin_tests_list <- list()

# prints one channel's pairwise tests table
print_violin_tables <- function(res) {
  cat("\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(
    res$tests %>%
      select(parameter, group1, group2, n1, n2, median1, median2,
             prob_1_greater, p_adj = p_adj_label, significance),
    digits = 4
  ))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

```{r plot-bootstrap-violins, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, results="asis"}
for (ch in unique(bootstrap_vs_single_fit$channel)) {

  # same cell lines as the bar plot above (H2B excluded, cell_lines_to_plot respected)
  lines_ch <- setdiff(
    select_cell_lines(unique(bootstrap_params$cell_line[bootstrap_params$channel == ch])),
    "H2B"
  )

  res <- bootstrap_violins_and_tests(
    bootstrap_params, param_cols_all, ch, lines_ch,
    title = paste0("Channel: ", ch, " - bootstrap distributions by cell line"),
    ylab  = "Value"
  )

  bootstrap_violin_tests_list[[length(bootstrap_violin_tests_list) + 1]] <-
    mutate(res$tests, plot = "fit parameters")

  print(res$plot)
  print_violin_tables(res)

  for (pl in plot_bootstrap_differences(res$diffs, res$tests, ch)) print(pl)
}
```

### Bootstrap: A_i and unrecovered fraction, each divided by (1 - C)

Same idea as the per-replicate version above, but for the bootstrap:
`A_i / (1 - C)` for each component actually present in `bootstrap_model`,
plus `frac_unrecovered = unrecovered_raw / (1 - C)` - together these sum
to 1. Bootstrap median ± SD is compared against the single fit to the
full average curve, exactly like the comparison above, just restricted to
this "divided by 1 - C" group of variables so it isn't mixed in with `C`,
`k_i`, and `tau_i` on very different scales.

```{r bootstrap-vs-single-fit-fractions}
param_cols_fractions <- bootstrap_params %>%
  select(matches("^frac_A[0-9]+$"), frac_unrecovered) %>%
  names()

bootstrap_fraction_stats <- bootstrap_params %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  select(cell_line, channel, all_of(param_cols_fractions)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(param_cols_fractions), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel, parameter) %>%
  summarize(
    bootstrap_median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    bootstrap_sd     = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

single_fit_fraction_params <- fit_results %>%
  filter(model == bootstrap_model, converged) %>%
  select(cell_line, channel, any_of(param_cols_fractions)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(cell_line, channel), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "single_fit_value")

bootstrap_vs_single_fit_fractions <- single_fit_fraction_params %>%
  inner_join(bootstrap_fraction_stats, by = c("cell_line", "channel", "parameter")) %>%
  mutate(
    diff                      = single_fit_value - bootstrap_median,
    z_single_fit_vs_bootstrap = diff / bootstrap_sd
  ) %>%
  arrange(cell_line, channel, parameter)

bootstrap_vs_single_fit_fractions %>% knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

```{r plot-bootstrap-vs-single-fit-fractions, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}

    geom_col(alpha = 0.6, width = 0.7) +

      width = 0.25, color = "#D95F02", linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_point(

    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste0("Channel: ", ch, " - A_i and unrecovered fraction (each / (1 - C))"),
      subtitle = "Bar + orange error bar = bootstrap median ± 1 SD; black diamond = single fit to the full average curve",
      x = "Cell line", y = "Value / (1 - C)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")

  print(p)
}
```
