### Bootstrap: focused pairwise comparisons (one PDF per metric per comparison)

Three focused comparisons - HOXC10 vs HOXC13, HOXC10 vs HOXC10-13-10, and
HOXC13 vs HOXC13-10-13 - each with **one violin plot per metric** (every
fit parameter such as `k1`, `k2`, `tau_1`, ..., plus the `/ (1 - C)`
fractions), using the colors defined in the Parameters section. Each plot
is shown below and also exported as its own PDF to
`pdf_figures/violin_comparisons/<comparison>/`.

**Statistical testing** (same scheme as the slow-recovery bootstrap script).
Each comparison is tested on only its two cell lines, with the same bootstrap
difference test as above (P(A > B) over all pairings, p = 2 × min(P, 1 − P),
floored at 1 / n). Within each comparison:

* **Holm family** (Holm-corrected together): `holm_params_focused` - C, the
  fractions frac_A1, frac_A2 (, frac_A3), frac_unrecovered and the time
  constants tau_1, tau_2 (, tau_3).
* **Tested, not corrected** (marked `°` on the plots): the raw amplitudes
  A1, A2 (, A3), the rates k1, k2 (, k3), and unrecovered_raw.
* **Not tested**: `untested_params_focused` (empty by default; any parameter
  listed there is still plotted, without a bracket).

There is no additional correction across the three comparisons. These tests
are also appended to `bootstrap_pairwise_cell_line_tests.csv` in the export
chunk below. These plots ignore `cell_lines_to_plot`.

```{r export-pairwise-violins, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=5}
violin_comparisons <- list(
  list(name = "HOXC10_vs_HOXC13",       lines = c("HOXC10", "HOXC13")),
  list(name = "HOXC10_vs_HOXC10-13-10", lines = c("HOXC10", "HOXC10-13-10")),
  list(name = "HOXC13_vs_HOXC13-10-13", lines = c("HOXC13", "HOXC13-10-13"))
)

# Holm family and untested parameters for the focused comparisons
holm_params_focused     <- c("C", "frac_A1", "frac_A2", "frac_A3", "frac_unrecovered",
                             "tau_1", "tau_2", "tau_3")
untested_params_focused <- character(0)

focused_metrics <- c(param_cols_all, param_cols_fractions)

# One violin plot for one metric of one comparison, with the (already
# corrected) test result of that metric as a single bracket.
plot_focused_violin <- function(long, tests_comp, metric, lines, title) {
  d <- long %>%
    filter(parameter == metric) %>%
    mutate(cell_line = factor(cell_line, levels = lines))
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)

  y_top <- max(d$value)
  step  <- max(diff(range(d$value)) * 0.08, abs(y_top) * 0.02, 1e-9)

  br <- tests_comp %>%
    filter(parameter == metric, !is.na(p_adj)) %>%
    mutate(x1 = 1, x2 = 2, y = y_top + step,
           label = paste0(significance, ifelse(in_holm, "", "°")))

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = cell_line, y = value, fill = cell_line)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.6, scale = "width", trim = TRUE, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.28,
                 fatten = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cell_line_colors) +
    # y axis goes down to (at least) 0
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = paste0(metric, ": ",
                           if (metric %in% untested_params_focused) "not tested"
                           else if (metric %in% holm_params_focused) "Holm-corrected"
                           else "uncorrected (°)"),
         x = NULL, y = metric) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")

  if (nrow(br) > 0) {
    p <- p +
      geom_segment(data = br, aes(x = x1, xend = x2, y = y, yend = y),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_text(data = br, aes(x = 1.5, y = y, label = label),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
      geom_blank(data = br, aes(x = 1.5, y = y + step), inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  p
}

focused_tests_list <- list()

for (ch in channels_to_model) {
  for (comp in violin_comparisons) {

    present <- intersect(
      comp$lines,
      unique(bootstrap_params$cell_line[bootstrap_params$channel == ch & bootstrap_params$converged])
    )

    if (length(present) < 2) {
      message(sprintf("Skipping %s, channel '%s': need both cell lines with kept bootstrap iterations.",
                      comp$name, ch))
      next
    }

    comp_dir <- file.path(pdf_export_folder, "violin_comparisons", comp$name)
    dir.create(comp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

    long <- bootstrap_params %>%
      filter(converged, channel == ch, cell_line %in% comp$lines) %>%
      select(cell_line, all_of(focused_metrics)) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = all_of(focused_metrics), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
      filter(is.finite(value))

    # all tests of this comparison first, then Holm over the Holm family only
    tests_comp <- bootstrap_pairwise_tests(
      long %>% filter(!parameter %in% untested_params_focused)
    ) %>%
      mutate(in_holm = parameter %in% holm_params_focused) %>%
      mutate(p_adj = {
        pa <- p_value                                    # not in the Holm family: uncorrected
        pa[in_holm] <- p.adjust(p_value[in_holm], method = "holm")
        pa
      }) %>%
      mutate(significance = p_to_stars(p_adj),
             p_adj_label  = ifelse(is.na(p_adj), NA_character_,
                                   paste0(ifelse(p_is_floor, "<", ""), sprintf("%.3g", p_adj))),
             channel = ch, .before = 1)

    for (metric in focused_metrics) {
      p <- plot_focused_violin(long, tests_comp, metric, comp$lines,
                               paste0(ch, " - ", comp$lines[1], " vs. ", comp$lines[2]))
      if (is.null(p)) next

      # show in the knitted document as well as saving the PDF
      print(p)
      ggsave(file.path(comp_dir, paste0(ch, "_", metric, ".pdf")),
             p, width = 4.5, height = 5, device = "pdf")
    }

    focused_tests_list[[length(focused_tests_list) + 1]] <-
      mutate(tests_comp, comparison = comp$name, plot = paste0("pairwise: ", comp$name))
  }
}

focused_tests <- bind_rows(focused_tests_list)

bootstrap_violin_tests_list[[length(bootstrap_violin_tests_list) + 1]] <- focused_tests

focused_tests %>%
  select(comparison, parameter, group1, group2, n1, n2, median1, median2,
         prob_1_greater, p_value, p_adj = p_adj_label, holm_corrected = in_holm, significance) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

### Bootstrap: composition of the recovery (C / 1 - C and stacked fractions)

For each of the three focused comparisons (`violin_comparisons` above), two
plots with one stacked bar per cell line, from the kept bootstrap iterations
of `bootstrap_model`:

* **C and 1 - C**: median of C, and 1 - median(C) on top, so each bar adds up
  to 1. Error bar: ± 1 SD of C across iterations, at the top of the C segment.
* **Fractions**: medians of the `frac_A*` columns (frac_A1 at the bottom) and
  `frac_unrecovered` on top. Each fraction's error bar (± 1 SD across
  iterations) is drawn at the top of its own segment. A negative median
  frac_unrecovered is not drawn (with a warning). Because each fraction's
  median is taken separately, the stack does not have to add up to exactly 1.

Both plots are shown below and exported as PDFs to
`pdf_figures/composition/<comparison>/`. These plots ignore
`cell_lines_to_plot`.

```{r composition-plots, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=5.5, results="asis"}
frac_A_cols <- sort(grep("^frac_A[0-9]+$", names(bootstrap_params), value = TRUE))
frac_comp   <- c(frac_A_cols, "frac_unrecovered")
frac_alpha  <- setNames(c(seq(1, 0.4, length.out = length(frac_A_cols)), 0.15), frac_comp)
C_alpha     <- c("C" = 0.9, "1 - C" = 0.25)

composition_stats <- bootstrap_params %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  group_by(cell_line, channel) %>%
  summarize(n_kept = n(),
            across(all_of(c("C", frac_comp)),
                   list(median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                   .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"),
            .groups = "drop")

cat("\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(composition_stats, digits = 4))
cat("\n\n")

# stacked bars drawn as rectangles: x = position of the cell line in the pair
stacked_plot <- function(seg, err, alpha_vals, title, ylab) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = seg, aes(xmin = x - 0.35, xmax = x + 0.35, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
                              fill = cell_line, alpha = component),
              color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_errorbar(data = err, aes(x = x, ymin = y - sd, ymax = y + sd),
                  width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(unique(seg$cell_line)),
                       labels = unique(seg$cell_line), expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cell_line_colors, guide = "none") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = alpha_vals, name = NULL,
                       guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey30"),
                                            reverse = TRUE)) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = paste0("Bootstrap ", bootstrap_model,
                                          ": median, error bar = ± 1 SD"),
         x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "right", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
}

for (ch in channels_to_model) {
  for (comp in violin_comparisons) {

    st <- composition_stats %>%
      filter(channel == ch, cell_line %in% comp$lines) %>%
      mutate(x = match(cell_line, comp$lines)) %>%
      arrange(x)
    if (nrow(st) < 2) {
      message(sprintf("Skipping composition plots for %s, channel '%s': need both cell lines.",
                      comp$name, ch))
      next
    }

    comp_dir <- file.path(pdf_export_folder, "composition", comp$name)
    dir.create(comp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

    # ---- C and 1 - C ----
    seg_C <- bind_rows(
      st %>% transmute(cell_line, x, component = "C",     ymin = 0,        ymax = C_median),
      st %>% transmute(cell_line, x, component = "1 - C", ymin = C_median, ymax = 1)
    ) %>% mutate(component = factor(component, levels = names(C_alpha)))
    err_C <- st %>% transmute(x, y = C_median, sd = C_sd)

    pC <- stacked_plot(seg_C, err_C, C_alpha,
                       paste0(ch, " - C and 1 - C: ", comp$lines[1], " vs. ", comp$lines[2]),
                       "Fraction of pre-bleach intensity")
    print(pC)
    cat("\n\n")
    ggsave(file.path(comp_dir, paste0(ch, "_C_composition.pdf")),
           pC, width = 4.5, height = 5.5, device = "pdf")

    # ---- fractions ----
    seg_list <- list(); err_list <- list()
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(st))) {
      cl  <- st$cell_line[j]
      med <- unlist(st[j, paste0(frac_comp, "_median")]); names(med) <- frac_comp
      sdv <- unlist(st[j, paste0(frac_comp, "_sd")]);     names(sdv) <- frac_comp

      comps <- frac_comp
      if (!is.finite(med[["frac_unrecovered"]]) || med[["frac_unrecovered"]] < 0) {
        warning(sprintf("%s (%s): median frac_unrecovered = %.4f is negative - not plotted.",
                        cl, ch, med[["frac_unrecovered"]]))
        comps <- setdiff(comps, "frac_unrecovered")
      }
      tops <- cumsum(med[comps])
      seg_list[[j]] <- tibble(cell_line = cl, x = st$x[j], component = comps,
                              ymin = c(0, head(tops, -1)), ymax = tops)
      err_list[[j]] <- tibble(x = st$x[j], y = tops, sd = sdv[comps])
    }
    seg_F <- bind_rows(seg_list) %>% mutate(component = factor(component, levels = frac_comp))
    err_F <- bind_rows(err_list)

    pF <- stacked_plot(seg_F, err_F, frac_alpha,
                       paste0(ch, " - fractions of the bleached amount: ",
                              comp$lines[1], " vs. ", comp$lines[2]),
                       "Fraction of 1 - C")
    print(pF)
    cat("\n\n")
    ggsave(file.path(comp_dir, paste0(ch, "_fractions_composition.pdf")),
           pF, width = 4.5, height = 5.5, device = "pdf")
  }
}
```

### Diagnostic: unique curves used per iteration

Curves are drawn **with replacement**, so each iteration's `x` draws
usually contain repeats. This plots how many *distinct* individual curves
actually went into each iteration's resampled average curve (out of `x`
total draws) - a low, erratic count would suggest the curve pool is too
small for the draws to be very independent of each other.

```{r plot-bootstrap-n-unique, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
for (cl in select_cell_lines(unique(bootstrap_params$cell_line))) {
  for (ch in unique(bootstrap_params$channel[bootstrap_params$cell_line == cl])) {

    df <- bootstrap_params %>% filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch)

    p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = iteration, y = n_unique_curves)) +
      geom_point(color = "#2C7FB8", size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
      labs(
        title = paste0("Cell line: ", cl, ", channel: ", ch,
                        " - unique curves drawn per bootstrap iteration"),
        subtitle = paste0(unique(df$n_curves_drawn), " curves drawn per iteration, with replacement"),
        x = "Iteration", y = "Number of unique curves"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()

    print(p)
  }
}
```

### Diagnostic: C and amplitude parameters across iterations

Plots `C` together with whichever amplitude terms (`A1`, `A2`, `A3`)
actually exist in `bootstrap_params` - i.e. only as many as
`bootstrap_model` has (one for mono-exponential, two for bi-exponential,
three for tri-exponential), so nothing errors if a term isn't there.

```{r plot-bootstrap-params-scatter, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
params_to_plot <- intersect(c("C", "A1", "A2", "A3", "tau_1", "tau_2", "tau_3"), names(bootstrap_params))

bootstrap_long_cA <- bootstrap_params %>%
  filter(converged) %>%
  select(cell_line, channel, iteration, all_of(params_to_plot)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(params_to_plot), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value")

for (cl in select_cell_lines(unique(bootstrap_long_cA$cell_line))) {
  for (ch in unique(bootstrap_long_cA$channel[bootstrap_long_cA$cell_line == cl])) {

    df <- bootstrap_long_cA %>% filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch)

    p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = iteration, y = value)) +
      geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.6, color = "#2C7FB8") +
      facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
      labs(
        title = paste0("Cell line: ", cl, ", channel: ", ch,
                        " - C and amplitude parameters across iterations"),
        x = "Iteration", y = "Parameter value"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()

    print(p)
  }
}
```



### Diagnostic: amplitude vs. inverse rate constant

For each iteration, plots `A1` against `1/k1`, `A2` against `1/k2`, and
`A3` against `1/k3` - each pair is skipped automatically if it doesn't
exist for the chosen model (e.g. `A2`/`k2` and `A3`/`k3` are both skipped
for a mono-exponential fit; only `A3`/`k3` is skipped for a bi-exponential
one), so nothing errors regardless of which model was fit.

```{r plot-bootstrap-amplitude-vs-invk, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
inv_k_pairs <- list(c("A1", "k1"), c("A2", "k2"), c("A3", "k3"))

for (pair in inv_k_pairs) {
  amp_col <- pair[1]
  k_col   <- pair[2]

  if (!all(c(amp_col, k_col) %in% names(bootstrap_params))) next

  df_pair <- bootstrap_params %>%
    filter(converged) %>%
    mutate(inv_k = 1 / .data[[k_col]])

  for (cl in select_cell_lines(unique(df_pair$cell_line))) {
    for (ch in unique(df_pair$channel[df_pair$cell_line == cl])) {

      df <- df_pair %>% filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch)

      if (nrow(df) == 0) next

      p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[amp_col]], y = inv_k)) +
        geom_point(color = "#31A354", size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(
          title = paste0("Cell line: ", cl, ", channel: ", ch,
                          " - ", amp_col, " vs. 1/", k_col),
          subtitle = "Each point is one bootstrap iteration",
          x = amp_col, y = paste0("1/", k_col)
        ) +
        theme_minimal()

      print(p)
    }
  }
}
```

```{r bootstrap-failed}
bootstrap_params %>%
  filter(!converged) %>%
  count(cell_line, channel, error, name = "n_iterations")
```

### Export bootstrap results

Saves the raw per-iteration parameters (one row per iteration, so you can
inspect the full distribution or re-plot it later), the median/SD summary
table, and the pairwise cell-line significance tests from the violin plots
to csv files in a `bootstrap_results` subfolder of `curve_folder`.

```{r export-bootstrap}
bootstrap_export_folder <- file.path(curve_folder, "bootstrap_results")
dir.create(bootstrap_export_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

for (cl in unique(bootstrap_params$cell_line)) {
  for (ch in unique(bootstrap_params$channel[bootstrap_params$cell_line == cl])) {
    out_file <- file.path(
      bootstrap_export_folder,
      paste0(cl, "_", ch, "_bootstrap_iterations.csv")
    )

    bootstrap_params %>%
      filter(cell_line == cl, channel == ch) %>%
      write_csv(out_file)
  }
}

summary_file <- file.path(bootstrap_export_folder, "all_cell_lines_bootstrap_summary.csv")
write_csv(bootstrap_summary, summary_file)

if (length(bootstrap_violin_tests_list) > 0) {
  write_csv(
    bind_rows(bootstrap_violin_tests_list),
    file.path(bootstrap_export_folder, "bootstrap_pairwise_cell_line_tests.csv")
  )
}

list.files(bootstrap_export_folder, full.names = TRUE)
```
